title: OptManager transactional rollback on OptionsError
answers: How does mitmproxy handle errors during options configuration?
What happens when an addon raises OptionsError during configure?
How does OptManager guarantee transactional option updates?
body:
Option updates in `mitmproxy/optmanager.py:OptManager` are atomic and transactional across all `.changed` signal listeners (e.g. addon `configure` hooks).
- When options are set via `OptManager.update` or attribute assignment, handlers attached to `OptManager.changed` execute.
- If any handler raises `mitmproxy/exceptions.py:OptionsError`, `OptManager` catches it, rolls back all option values to their state prior to the transaction, suppresses the exception, and notifies `OptManager.errored`.
- Skipping `OptionsError` and letting another exception escape will bypass rollback and leave options in a partially updated state. Option attributes must not be mutated in-place; `OptManager` returns deep copies on attribute access.
applies: When updating options or implementing addon configure hooks
says: Applying invalid proxy settings leaves configuration in a half changed broken state.
Settings should automatically revert to previous values if an error occurs while saving.
Entering an invalid option value causes subsequent configuration changes to behave unpredictably.
Ensure configuration changes roll back cleanly when an extension rejects new options.
